scope: Local source, synthetic API/tenant, policy, build, and browser verification for the fail-closed API route authorization contract.

enforcedBehaviors: Application route registration fails when a method/template is absent from the typed security inventory.
Identity and tenant routes verify the bearer identity before handler execution.
Tenant routes resolve active membership server-side and enforce every declared permission before handler execution.
Request-local identity and tenant authority are reused while handler-level permission checks remain in place.
Provider webhook routes remain bound to their exact-body Shopify or Stripe signature services.
Missing or invalid authentication returns 401; authenticated foreign membership and insufficient permission return the same 404 contract.

verification.command: pnpm exec vitest run --project unit --project tenant apps/api/src

targetedAssertions: The source and typed manifest contain the same 44 unique routes.
Each tenant manifest permission set exactly equals its handler-level authorizeRequest/requirePermission literals.
Public, identity, and provider-signature handlers contain no tenant permission call.
Generated HEAD routes reuse only the reviewed GET contract; unknown methods and paths are rejected.
Unauthenticated tenant access returns 401 without membership lookup.
Authenticated foreign-tenant access returns the same bounded 404 as insufficient permission and does not invoke the repository.
Identity and membership resolution run once per authorized request.
The privacy evidence package retains both retention:manage and data:export admission.
limitations: This is local source and synthetic evidence, not a penetration test or production certification.
No current live PostgreSQL, reverse-proxy, multi-replica, staging adversarial, or response-timing exercise was available.
Repository predicates, PostgreSQL RLS, BFF CSRF/origin controls, and provider signature validation remain independently required.
No Git commit, push, publication, or deployment was performed.
